memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"This observance will be for you like a sign on your hand and a reminder on your
forehead that this law of the LORD is to be on your lips. For the LORD brought
you out of Egypt with his mighty hand. You must keep this ordinance at the
appointed time year after year." - Ex 13:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A sign on the hand and a reminder on the forehead. The hand is what we do. The
forehead is what we think. God wants His deliverance to shape both.

Some Jewish practice took this literally, binding small boxes of Scripture to
the arm and head, and Jesus gently criticised the way some had turned this into
display (Matt 23:5). Whether taken literally or as a vivid picture, the meaning
is the same: let this truth govern your actions and your thoughts.

Notice the third element: "on your lips." Hand, head, and mouth. What we do,
what we think, what we say. God is after the whole person, not a compartment of
religious activity.

This is where much of our struggle sits. We can hold sound beliefs in our heads
while our hands do something else. Or we can be busy in service while our
thought life goes untended. Paul prays for believers to be transformed "by the
renewing of your mind" (Rom 12:2), because what settles in the mind eventually
reaches the hands.

And notice the rhythm: "year after year." Not a one-time surge of devotion, but
a lifelong pattern. God builds His people through repetition.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there a gap between what you believe and what you do?
2. What regular rhythm keeps God's truth in front of you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, take my hands, my thoughts, and my words. Let Your truth shape all of me,
not just part of me. Amen.
